name: EPL key-starter absence -> team xG base rates

data.source: understat.com getLeagueData/EPL/<season> (fixtures, team xG) and getMatchData/<id> (rosters)

FB: MR/ML when the XI has exactly 3 DC and no DR/DL/DMR/DML (wing-backs)

definitions.position_source: Understat starting formation slot of each match
definitions.key_starter: started >= 60% of the team's league matches that season (any slot); assigned to the position group where most of his starts were (modal group). Spec-literal rule (>= 60% in one group) reported under robustness.strict_key_rule.
definitions.absence: a key starter who is not in that match's starting XI (injury, suspension, rotation, or not yet signed / already left)

tiers.start_share: core: started >= 80% of team league matches; regular: 60%-80%
tiers.attack_rank: top3: top-3 in team-season (xG+xA)/90 among players with >= 900 league minutes

model.equation: xg_for[t,m] = a[team-season] + d[opp-season] + h*home + sum_g b_for[g]*n_absent_own[g] + sum_g b_against[g]*n_absent_opp[g] + e
model.note: one row per team per match; b_for = change in the absent team's xG-for per absent key starter; b_against = change in the absent team's xG-against (estimated from the opponent's rows). Equivalent to separate xG-for and xG-against regressions with team-season FE, opponent-season FE, home, own absences, each also controlling for the other side's absences.
model.se: clustered by the absent team's team-season (se_*); se_twoway_* also clusters by the other team-season

out_of_sample.design: coefficients fit on train seasons; on test seasons the baseline (team-season + opp-season FE + home) is cross-fitted with 10 folds by match, so every test match is predicted from FE estimated without it. Model A = baseline; model B = baseline re-fitted on y minus the train-season absence offset, plus that offset. Loss = squared error of per-team-match xG. CI clusters by team-season (or by match, whichever is wider).

usage.defence_multiplier: 1 + sum_i d_xg_against[group_i] / base_xg_against   (applied to the opponent's expected xG)
usage.multiplicative_alternative: prod_i (1 + pct_xg_for_ppml[group_i]/100)  -- same idea on the log scale
recommended_lookup: default: base_rates.by_group (all 12 seasons), d_xg_for for the absent team's attack, d_xg_against for its defence
known undisputed starter (started >= 80% when the season ends up counted) -> by_group_x_start_share_tier 'core'; known top-3 attacker of the team -> by_group_x_attack_rank_tier 'top3'
a winger in a front three (Understat FWL/FWR) sits in ST in by_group; for role-based lookup use by_group_alt_fwl_fwr_as_wide

xG-against side: 2022-25 effects are about twice the 2014-21 ones (robustness.era_split_any_key_starter; OOS calibration slope > 1 for the xG-against terms); by_group_recent_2022_25 is the recent-era alternative with larger SE
if the CI covers 0, treat the effect as 'small, sign uncertain', not as zero evidence of no effect

worked_example.case: team baseline xG-for 1.60, xG-against 1.10; its key ST and key CB are both out

usage.baseline_caveat: Coefficients are relative to all key starters starting. A baseline fitted on past results (M) already contains the team's typical absences (key starters miss ~20% of matches), so relative to such a baseline use d * (1 - p), p = that player's usual absence rate (default 0.2).

limitations: Endogeneity: rotation concentrates in matches against weak opponents and in congested weeks; opponent-season FE absorbs average opponent strength only, and European/cup fixtures are not in the data (rest-day control uses league fixtures only).
Injury, suspension and tactical rotation are not separated; did_not_play_only is the closest proxy for injury/suspension.

Dead rubbers and within-season form changes (manager sackings) are not modelled directly; drop_each_team_last5 and recent_form_controls (previous-5-match xG form of both sides) leave the estimates essentially unchanged.

Placebo: the match BEFORE an absence already shows part of the effect. Most of it sits in matches where the player was subbed off before 85' (in-match injury: the disruption starts in that match), but for defenders who played the full 90 the next-match absence still predicts +0.07 xG-against in the current match (cards/knocks picked up under pressure, or selection). Defensive coefficients may therefore be somewhat overstated; the GK estimate is the least trustworthy.

Era shift: absence effects on xG-against in 2022-25 are about 2x those of 2014-21 (any key starter +0.099 vs +0.049 per absence); the cause is not identified (five-substitute rule, style, sample noise).
Tiers are noisier than the pooled group estimates; GK 'regular' (60-80% starts) > 'core' is consistent with keepers being dropped after poor spells, i.e. selection.
Key status uses the whole season (look-ahead); out_of_sample.no_lookahead_key_status_second_half tests status from the first 19 matches only.
Replacement quality is not modelled: the coefficient is the average net effect after the manager's replacement choice.
Understat position labels are formation slots; wide forwards in a front three are FWL/FWR (ST group), wing-backs follow the back-three rule.
Absences include matches before a mid-season signing's arrival (see key_starter_summary.absences_before_first_appearance_fraction).
